response_strategy:
This DREF allocation aims to deliver humanitarian assistance to at risk communities under the following strategic areas: 

1. Vaccination campaign: Support the outbreak response immunization (ORI) activities of the Ministry of Health in selected 5 locations through the social mobilization of trained Red Crescent volunteers during the two-week period at the end of September 2023. 

2. Working with the parents and caregivers of zero-dose and under-immunized children to reduce their vaccine hesitancy and encourage them to vaccinate their children against measles. 

3. Public education to improve people’s awareness on the importance of vaccinating their children against measles, through active engagement of communities.
people_assisted:
The DREF operation targets the following groups: 
1) Groups most at risk for measles - children from 9 months to 84 months-old children (under 8 years) in the most affected regions (Chui region, Bishkek city, Osh city, Osh region, Jalal-Abad city). 602,000 children
2)  Vaccine - hesitant parents and caregivers who have refused vaccination (zero -dose children and under-immunized children) 
3) Parents of preschool children and school-aged children (0 and 1st grade), 
4) Teachers of kindergartens and 0 and 1 classes,
5) Community Leaders,
6) General population.

The target groups 3-6 as listed above are the same as those indicated in the Ministry of Health's communication plan for the current measles situation. The above groups in the selected regions are estimated to be around 800,000. The awareness campaign plans to cover up to 10% of the total group, or 80,000 people.

The selected regions and cities for this operation (Osh, Jalal-Abad and Chu regions and Bishkek and Osh cities) are the most affected regions. Jalal-Abad city is added as the additional, fifth location considering the evolving epidemiological situation.
operation_objective: The overall objective of the operation is to reduce the impact of the current increase of measles cases on the most vulnerable, at-risk groups with the aim of reducing morbidity and mortality in coordination with the government health structures. The operation aims to reach a total of 80,000 people in the selected communities through improving the awareness of parents and caregivers of children aged 9-84 months (under 8 years) on the importance and safety of measles vaccination, supporting social mobilization efforts during the planned immunization campaign in September 2023 and tackling vaccine hesitancy among the parents and caregivers of zero-dose and under-immunized children.
pmer:
Monitoring and evaluation are an integral part of the operation and are carried out involving the assisted people and other stakeholders utilizing participatory approaches throughout the operation’s timeframe. Regular internal monthly operation updates are developed by the project team and shared with the IFRC Regional Office for Europe.  
Meetings with key stakeholders and field visits are done on a regular basis to monitor the implementation progress. 
RCSK is planning to organize its lesson learned workshop at the end of the operation to evaluate key achievements and challenges in order to improve the National Society response operations in the future. 
Regular coordination meetings are held with the regional health authorities to determine the level of increase in the vaccine coverage rates following the risk communication and outreach activities by the Red Crescent volunteers.
major_coordination_mechanism: The Republican Center of Immunoprophylaxis established an operation center to coordinate the efforts in response to this situation. The RCSK remains in close coordination with the RCI and organized several meetings to coordinate its response activities.
event_description:
According to the Republican Center for Immunoprophylaxis (RCI) of the Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic, since the beginning of 2023, the epidemiological situation in the country for measles and rubella has deteriorated. The first cases were reported in the first epidemiological week in Bishkek city and Chui regions, and, starting from the eighth epidemiological week, it has spread to Osh city and Osh region. Later, it has spread to an additional 34 districts in five (5) regions. 

As of 13 November 2023, according to the Republican Center for Immunoprophylaxis, 3,618 cases of measles have been detected since the beginning of 2023. 
The distribution of measles cases across the country is as follows: 
- Bishkek city - 1,076 cases, 
- Osh city - 333 cases, 
- Osh region - 695 cases, 
- Batken region - 96 cases, 
- Chui region - 562 cases,
- Jalal-Abad region - 650 cases, 
- Talas region- 95 cases,
- Issyk-Kul region- 72 cases, 
- Naryn region - 39 cases. ⠀

In terms of age distribution, 88% or 3,195 cases are children under 10 years old. By vaccination status, 87% or 3,140 cases were unvaccinated for various reasons. Active circulation of measles virus is observed in Bishkek, Jalal-Abad and Chui oblasts, where transmission occurs among unvaccinated children in institutions (schools, kindergartens, etc.). (Source: https://med.kg/pressCenter/news/eebaed63-4ed7-4e9a-ab1f-18c1851c231b?locale=ru)

On 30 October, two secondary schools in Jalal-Abad city were closed following the registration of measles cases. The region's epidemiological services decided to hold educational processes in an online format. 

For comparison, 23 cases of measles were reported nationwide in 2022, three (3) cases in 2021 and 733 cases in 2020 in Kyrgyzstan. In 2019, the WHO recognized Kyrgyzstan as a rubella-free country (Source: https://www.unicef.org/kyrgyzstan/press-releases/european-immunization-week-kyrgyzstan-every-vaccine-dose-matters-protect-you-and). The country has experienced a large measles outbreak in 2014-2015, when 17,779 measles cases were reported.

Reduced vaccine coverage rates for childhood vaccinations during the COVID-19 pandemic played a key role in the current increase of measles cases in Kyrgyzstan. 

The Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic notes that during the COVID-19 pandemic, routine vaccination coverage has significantly dropped. In 2021, coverage in the Kyrgyz Republic with the first dose of MMR was 93.3%, and coverage with the second dose of MMR was 96.9%. In 2022, coverage in the republic with the first dose of MMR was 94.4%, and coverage with the second dose of MMR was 94.5%.

The vaccine coverage rates for measles-containing vaccines are below the WHO recommended levels, especially in Bishkek city, Osh, Batken, and Jalal-Abad regions. To reduce the burden of measles, the WHO recommends coverage of ≥ 95% of two doses of Measles Containing Vaccine (MCV) to assure immune response and interrupt the transmission. While the vaccine coverage rates have increased in the past two years, it remains below the pre-pandemic levels. 

As expected, the number of cases started to rise from September, with the start of the academic year, when all schools and kindergartens reopened. Also, as the temperature is dropping below zero degrees and people are remaining indoors for extended periods of time, the number of cases is increasing. During the flu season in the fall and winter, the health services become overstretched dealing with a large number of children with ARI. Compounding the problem is the existing levels of malnutrition among children: 11% of children 0 - 4 years are stunted (2020), 1% severe wasted and 2% moderately wasted (2015 - 2020).

national_society_actions.title: national_society_eoc
national_society_actions.description: Due to the scope and extent of the structured fires SARCS activated its National Response Team (NRT) and Emergency Operation Centre (EOC). The NRT closely coordinates the operation interventions with the Provincial Response Team (PRT) which also ensures that the Branch Response Teams (BRT) are well coordinated and provide timely updates. Internal coordination of logistics, communication and any skill gaps that might be identified are easily addressed through the established coordination system which strengthens SARCS capacity on major response of this nature.

national_society_actions.title: resource_mobilization
national_society_actions.description:
There has been efforts to mobilise resources in country since the event occurred but there has been minimal support from all angles especially with the fact that most affected people are external migrants from countries like Malawi, Tanzania, Zimbabwe to mention but a few. Most resources that have been received has been in kind donations of recycled clothing. SARCS managed to distribute blankets and mattresses, but the stock has depleted as they have been responding to sporadic structure fires especially in informal settlements since the onset of winter.

Due to limited support from in country government, corporates and donors, SARCS is reaching out to Red Cross and Red Cresent (RCRC) Movement partners for support to assist the affected people through launching of Disaster Relief Emergency Fund (DREF).

national_society_actions.description:
- SARCS continues to facilitate its participatory approach of Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) with affected communities. 
- Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) and Protection, Gender, and Inclusion (PGI) are integral components of all response interventions, especially following the potential challenges in the migrant situation and the need to have leaders involved and advocating on the same efforts (both at community and local authorities level). 
- The NS is in constant communication with community leaders of different nationalities to also ensure that communication reaches everyone and that there is no language barrier as the community leaders will be able to translate any communication to their community members. The NS will also continue to engage the government to ensure that advocacy for the undocumented migrants is strengthened because they will really have nowhere to go after they are turned away from the shelters.
- There have been special effort as well on NS advocacy for Government shelter support to the communities affected in the different fire incidents but also engagement on the need to strengthen the PGI minimum standards in the hosting centers. This come with initial positive outcomes and messages is passed for gender consideration in each centers and separation is done accordingly for all the established facilities.

Community participation and involvement will be prioritized, using existing community structures and engaging key stakeholders like community leaders. Special considerations will be given to individuals with specific needs.

national_society_actions.title: assessment
national_society_actions.description:
The South African Red Cross Society (SARCS) resumed assessments from onset to identified the needs and scale-up the response plan. Following the two incidents, rapid assessment were conducted and monitoring continues on any update on the situation and partners actions. 
- Form 16 to 17 th of July 2023 and assessment cover the fire outbreak of Kennedy road . 
- 31 August 2023 SARCS deployed a team that continues to collaborate with government disaster management teams to conduct assessments.  

The organization has been conducting joint assessments with government through its local municipality and disaster management center at district level. SARCS will continue to actively participate in Joint Operations Committee (JOC) which are spearheaded by the district municipality Disaster Management Centre (DMC) to ensure well-coordinated response and recovery interventions which minimize duplication of efforts to the same community. Since the devastating incident of the structured fires, South African Red Cross Society (SARCS) mobilized 20 volunteers and 10 staff members in Kennedy road and 20 more in Johannesburg incidents.

national_society_actions.title: shelter_housing_and_settlements
national_society_actions.description: SARCS deployed a team for initial distribution of 100 mattresses and 100 blankets from NS stock to be replenished under this intervention.

national_society_actions.title: coordination
national_society_actions.description:
SARCS National Response Team (NRT) was activated on the 30th of August 2023 to ensure proper coordination of response interventions internally. The Emergency Operation Centre (EOC) greatly assist in ensuring continues data monitoring and timely updates of information received from the field. Sharing of timely updates with the Head of Operation and technical team to inform decision making on response strategy and mechanisms.

SARCS Head quarters, Gauteng Provincial and Johannesburg branch activated a total of 20 staff and 30 volunteers to provide integrated response interventions. So far the NS team managed to provide First Aid, Restoring Family Links (RFL), Psychosocial Support Services, clothes and blankets. The team resumed needs assessments to get more understanding of the plight of survivors.

The response teams are responsible for ensuring SARCS participation, coordination and collaboration with government and other stakeholders at all levels. This ensures proper coordination of interventions to avoid duplication. SARCS has been active in the KZN province to respond to current crisis caused by the fires and has activated 20 volunteers and 10 staff members to conduct assessments, provide immediate relief and support services to affected people. So far, SARCS has provided 1,250 people with relief which include hot meals, clothes, blankets, mattress, Psychosocial Fist Aid (PFA) and Restoring Family links. Additional people are still not covered.

needs_identified.title: community_engagement_and_accountability
needs_identified.description:
Community Engagement and Accountability has been at the core of SARCS response interventions. Most affected people are hesitant to engage with government officials in fear of their status of migrant in irregular situation. However, they have been free to engage with non-governmental organizations like SARCS and share their plight. 

The rise of the fire in South Africa informal settlements have to be analyzed to understand the context and the potential factor. The origin of the current fire is not yet official but from the media, it is not a natural fire. The conditions of the affected settlements are then one of the factors to be analyzed for the identification if key actions, messages and sustainable intervention to build a community aware of key preventive and response actions that will contribute to reduce the risk of such event to happen or to have this scale. Indeed, such neighborhoods like the Kennedy settlement are characterized by the absence of clean, safe, reliable, affordable and environmentally friendly energy. Shortage of reliable energy is prevalent in under-resourced communities and is also a key contributor to the problem. This exposes these communities to untamed fires vulnerabilities which are mainly caused by paraffin stoves, heaters, and candle mishap. Sometimes fuels are also burnt in inefficient, leaky and unstable appliances, leading to health losses from pollutant emissions, burns, and conflagrations.  
Although structured fires have been a hazard to many of the informal settlements, the recent fires that blazed Kennedy Road informal settlement hit the area massively for the first time. This event is ringing the alert on such events, the place of the communities, government agencies and fire agencies in reducing the incidence/impact when this happens or reduce the factors bringing to those situations. 
Hence, there is need for intensive stakeholder engagements with regards to risks and vulnerabilities which most informal settlement in urban and peri-urban areas are exposed to. Enforcement of by-laws is necessary to ensure people settle in less risky areas. 
There is a need to sensitized people about building and using better materials to construct their homes. It is equally most needed for these communities to have plans and strategies in place that can minimize the risk of fires breaking out and causing total property destruction.

needs_identified.title: water_sanitation_and_hygiene
needs_identified.description:
Good hygiene practices are lacking due to limited materials especially among women and girls. There is need for provision of hygiene kits to the affected people.
Safe water is not coming to the priority need. Being in urban areas and relocated not far from the affected settlements, most have access to tape water that was already available before the fire and still be accessible. The hygiene kits will also facilitate water storage.
Affected people are in great need of hygiene packs and adolescents girls, youth and women require urgent supply of sanitary towels.

needs_identified.title: shelter_housing_and_settlements
needs_identified.description:
- In Johannesburg fire, the 175 families are placed across 3 shelters namely, Impilo (20), Khayalethu (36), and Hofland (147) as some of the people have gone to seek refuge with friends but we remain in communication with them. Other affected people are hesitant to join the shelters because of their irregular migration status in country and they fear that they will be deported. There is great need for provision of hygiene kits to the affected people.

- Following the fire outbreak of July in KwaZulu Natal, Kennedy Road, the families were relocated in informal settlements and host families around and lack minimum households' items to protect themselves. So far it has been determined that 98% of the affected people are non-citizens whom most of them are not having identification documents and their status in country is . This is causing some of the affected people to be hesitant to go to evacuation centres which have been established as shelters to accommodate the affected people.

In Kennedy Road, and Johannesburg, the affected population and families are in need for essential household items such as blankets, mattresses especially with the current cold experienced in the season. 

In the NS plan, the shelter construction is not covered as that need can only be covered through sustainable building which requires government to allocate safe spaces for displaced households currently in evacuation centers. This means that the need for now is for sustainable housing interventions by the government to ensure people's risks to hazards of this nature are minimized.  In his auxiliary role, NS will keep engaging government and partners to achieve that. Furthermore, there is a great need for building back better campaigns to ensure that the affected community is aware of safe building requirements and training of staff and volunteers on fire awareness so that they can continue raising awareness in the communities and avoid or reduce the impact of fire disasters should they happen again.

needs_identified.title: multi_purpose_cash_grants
needs_identified.description:
Although the affected people have received in kind donations like blankets, recycled clothes and currently hot meals, there is need to provide cash grants for them to be able to prioritize their needs and restore their dignity. It would be very helpful if the affected people could receive food vouchers for them to be able to get food parcels from selected food stores.
In the need analysis and possible intervention analysis, it is important to mention the repetitive fire recorded in recent months and beyond which has significantly impacted partners assistance capacity, including government shelter assistance. Additionally, multiple needs expressed include shelter and other sectors. In a context where the recently affected in Johannesburg are 98% undocumented migrants, there is a level of sensitivity that also need to be considered. There have been some violence incidents on assistance to recent fire affected communities while previous were still waiting for shelter support. A situation that is likely driven by the limited shelter assistance as of now. 
With that said, a consideration of the above-mentioned sensitivity and potential inter-community conflict there is at the same time a required neutrality and a need for humanitarian priorities in limited resources to face these recurrent events. Hence, the SARCS will opt for a multipurpose cash to give the communities the possibility to make their priorities without bringing the subject of complaints up.

needs_identified.title: protection_gender_and_inclusion
needs_identified.description: With a disaster of this nature where for example in Johannesburg 12 children have died amongst the 76 people reported and where others are hospitalized, it's important to prioritize child safeguarding to ensure that those children who are separated from their parents are profiled and referred to relevant Departments that can offer them more support. There is more importance that needs to be emphasized on SGBV prevention and mitigation especially with people being confined in evacuation centers.

needs_identified.title: livelihoods_and_basic_needs
needs_identified.description:
People's livelihoods have been greatly affected as the affected people have lost all their belongings to the fire blaze. Basic needs like food and clothing are greatly needed by the displaced people. 
SARCS has been providing hot meals to 1,500 people at the first days of Kennedy fire and extending it to the overall affected families. Stocks for that meals were limited, hence justifying support from the DREF. People are still in the evacuation centers and informal town hall areas. With limited resources,  the stock levels are depleting and there is a risk of the affected people being exposed to more vulnerabilities as they try to fend for themselves. In total 2,357 people are in need of immediate food assistance and NS needs to extend to the overall affected people with the hot meal provision.

All the hot meal distribution engaged by NGO latest fire are limited to that one meal provision. There is great need to provide food to the affected people as they have lost all their belongings. This represent a hot meal provision for these 175 families. 

There is a need to complement that provision. In addition, there is a challenge with baby food for infants in these early days. Even if the NS is providing hot meals, these does no cover specific needs for babies and infants.

For the rural area of Kennedy, people seeking solution for their own livelihood and food provision as per initial assessment are still lacking equipment to cook for themselves, neither houses or commodities to be able to cook for themselves at the moment. However, most expressed the need to get the kitchen sets in initial assessment and this remains. This will allow them to cook for themselves in few weeks to make it when they will move out of the evacuation centers.

needs_identified.title: health
needs_identified.description: MHPSS services are vital to address the emotional and psychological trauma experienced by the affected individuals and communities. The devastating loss of homes and belongings, along with the displacement and uncertainty, can have severe and long-lasting effects on mental health.

summary_of_change:
Fire incident have been recently more recurrent in South Africa, with more incident reported in informal settlements in Semi-urban or rural areas. The last fire outbreak was recorded in Kennedy road and SARCS initiated a response complemented by the IFRC support through a DREF allocation. The intervention ongoing, the Johannesburg fire was reported on 30.08.2023, requiring to extend the assistance to the affected communities following that tragedy. 
This update aim to provide details on the assistance that is planned by South Africa Red Cross on the ongoing needs expressed by the affected families following Johannesbourg fire incident while giving and update on the assistance provided in Durban after fire broke out in KwaZulu Natal on 16th July. Main highlights of this update are as follow:
- KwaZulu asisstance ongoing since 16 july 2023: SARCS has been with the communities affected by all the recent fires from the onsets include the Kennedy fire out of the scope of this DREF. The hot meal distribution started from the early hours following the disaster and continue over the past weeks. Following DREF support, SARCS also mobilized, trained and deploy 30 branches staff and volunteers that are currently ensuring awareness and PFA in the evacuation sites where the communities are still hosted. Relief support to 1,213 HHs as per initial target will be soon released with the procurement yet to be completed.

- On the new fire incident in Johannesburg, SARCS has also deploy the team for rapid provision of hot meals while ensuring rapid assessment and coordination with municipalities on possible actions. Hence, This DREF operation is revised to cover the immediate lifesaving of 175 households affected following the fire outbreak. These changes include:
• Extending for 3 months the intervention timeframe.
• An additional allocation of CHF 161,908 to enable immediate humanitarian assistance as per initial plan to be extended to the 175 HHs affected. This includes the emergency health, nutrition and essential items distribution to benefit 422 people.
• With consideration of the rural areas, sensitivity of the context and expressed multi-sectoral needs, a multipurpose cash is included for the Johannesburg assistance that will contribute to the families to access to their priority needs or cover existing gaps in the course of any additional assistance from stakeholders.

The NS will also continue to work with government departments to ensure that they are also up to date with any information with regards to the affected population especially with the reported incidents/grievance and claims that have characterized the assistance to the previous distributions and tentative (from government) in Durban fire and the others recent fire incidents like Kennedy, Johannesburg.
identified_gaps:
In general, support is needed to ensure sustainable shelter interventions that might not be able to be address through this DREF but at least, maximizing advocacy engagements for government to provide safe space for people to rebuild safer structures.
Also, although it is acknowledged that all affected people require assistance, it should be noted that the government has only profiled citizens for potential relief which might come from the government and will not be able to give to undocumented non-citizens who constitute 98% of the affected population in Johannesburg.
icrc:
The first aid kit refills which ICRC provided early this year as part of readiness interventions for incidents and disasters have been useful for the teams to provide first aid services during these early days of response. The teams collaboratively work with government paramedics to ensure urgent cases are attended to by professionals.
ICRC is currently supporting SARCS to intensify its PFL services to the affected people. In addition there has been efforts by Forensic team of ICRC in engaging the South African government to be given permission to assist in facilitating processing that can assist with establishing identification of the deceased whose identity is not yet known.
selection_criteria:
The operation is currently targeting all the people affected.
As part of CEA approach, SARCS will conduct a verification process which will engage key role players like Department of Social Development (DSD) and traditional/local leadership council to verify the selected households to ensure that the selection criteria are respected and properly followed. In addition, the selection assistance contain will be shared widely through trusted channels of communication which include community engagement forums which are usually spearheaded by traditional leaders and local authorities to ensure that people understand why and what is delivered by the NS. 

The targeting of overall affected is based on needs identified for all the families that lost their houses but also to minimize community tensions. 
National Society staff and volunteers will also collect feedback and complaints of targeted households during the selection and throughout the operation, based on the channels identified during the needs assessment as preferred by the affected communities. Feedback will be shared and analyzed at HQ to refine the selection process and criteria if necessary and ensure that complaints regarding the selection of community members are investigated and addressed in a timely manner. This feedback will also be used to adapt the intervention based on community needs, attitudes and perceptions.
ifrc:
The Pretoria Cluster Delegation continues to provide technical assistance to SARCS through reviewing of DREF application and general support towards the response.
A surge will be called-up to complement the delegation and cover the monitoring of activities in respective branches.
risk_security_concern: The affected area is an informal settlement and requires careful analysis of response measures to ensure it will not brew social unrest/violence as everyone would want to benefit.
national_authorities:
- The government so far has ensured that people who are displaced in a community hall and has managed to provide mobile toilet facilities to assist the affected people.
- The government through the City of Johannesburg Metro has requested support from non-governmental organizations to assist affected people to meet their basic needs.
- Government local authorities is leading the shelter decision and actions.
communication: SARCS has a communications unit, which works closely with different media houses to ensure that SARCS interventions are well published, and communities and stakeholders are aware of SARCS readiness and early action interventions. Updates on the operation will be shared on the National Society social media networks (websites, Facebook, Twitter). The National Society will also collaborate closely with IFRC communication focal person for technical support to ensure sufficient media coverage of the response. Operations teams will utilize visibility clothing and equipment during the operations to ensure easy identification and avoid harm. Both the SARCS and IFRC communications officers will be actively engaged to ensure proximity support to the operation. Since the South African Weather Services has warned that the rains will continue to pour, SARCS provincial and branch managers will convey early warning messages in the communities through loudhailers, group WhatsApp messages and local Radio interviews.
surge_personnel_deployed: Through this revision, a surge will be deployed. The preferable profile will look into the Disaster management coordination with skills on urban Disaster and shelter component. This profile will contribute to the direct discussions and capacity building of the NS on fire management, provide technical guidance to the NS during operations on specific shelter issues/discussions. The incumbent will guide the Shelter Sector and provide recommendations for DREF operation. Surge will enhance coordination of NS within country Department of Human settlement. The person deployed will give the technical oversights on the shelter/housing/settlements discussions as well as supporting the orientation on the advocacy efforts engaged and upcoming. Liaising the partners initiatives if any, to complement the existing assistance.
partner_national_society:
Currently there are no PNS involved who have contributed directly to this response at the moment. 
Recent supports include Belgian Red Cross support in recent floods response recovery interventions with provision of mobile kitchens for SARCS to be able to provide timely hot meals has greatly assisted during this fire response to ensure that people who are displaced are served with fresh meals.
event_scope:
The two fire outbreaks were respectively reported in different context that influence the response approach and also play a key role on the scope and complexity of each situation. SARCS analysis based on rapid assessments, coordination and monitoring is taking into consideration each scope as follows: 
A- First in Kennedy road - Kwazulu Natal in Durban (On the 16th of July 2023).
This was the worst fire incident in recent years in the area with about 2,357 people have been affected and displaced, being 647 children and 1,710 adults. This represents in 1,213 families. The devastating fire, which broke out on that day, resulted in complete destruction to more than 1,101 houses, leaving over a thousand people displaced, 02 fatalities and some reported injuries. SARCS KZN provincial response team rapid assessments of 17 July revealed also that: more than 1,101 households have seen their houses destroyed; 112 houses partially destroyed. 

B- Second in Johannesburg city, rural area. 
422 people were affected, representing 175 households now homeless. The assessments from both NS and from other sources have shown that 98% of the affected population are undocumented migrants and of these 72% are men. In most cases like these, these men are usually the breadwinners who are financially supporting their families back home and by virtue of them being undocumented it means they have no bank accounts which implies that they keep their money for remittances with them and any other things that they would have bought but due to the fires, they are left with absolutely nothing except the clothes they escaped the fire with.
The few women that are there are equally vulnerable because they would have lost everything as well in the fire and by virtue of them resorting to living in such a dilapidated building it shows that they have very low sources of income so this fire makes them even more vulnerable as they will not have anywhere to go at all after this and might have lost their jobs as well as they are trying to figure out tentative accommodation considering most undocumented migrants are not formally employed. 

In both situation, people who were affected by the fire incident were evacuated to centers, commonly local community/public areas whilst waiting for assistance and support. A lot of women, unaccompanied children especially in Johannesburg were affected. This incident brings up the need for food and water immediate and in coming weeks, school uniforms water supply, hygiene packs, mental health support and other Essential household items (EHI) etc. The stress and the losses recorded justify the level of needs. 

These families represent also hundreds of children homeless and facing breakage on their school cursus with the loss recorded and income impact. Immediate WASH interventions are essential to ensure access to clean water, sanitation facilities, and hygiene materials, which are critical in preventing the spread of diseases and promoting health in the affected areas.

The trauma and impact of this situation is significant with a scale never experienced, especially in Kwa Zulu even with the fire incidents recorded in the past 3 years. The affected population has never raised to this level. The most significant incidents were in August 2020 with successive fire experienced on 24 August 2020, in Kwa Zulu Natal where informal settlements In Mungeni Local Municipality 255 households were affected and under uMgungundlovu District Municipality and eThekwini Metro Municipality in Durban 267 households (482 people) were affected.  On 31 August 2020 in Johannesburg, Gauteng province, untamed fires were experienced in the informal settlements of Booysens and Diepsloot. The fire incident in Diepsloot resulted from a candle that was left unattended in one of the shacks. In Booysens, the fire was the result of arson as two men were fighting, and one suspect sought revenge by burning the shack of the other rival.  The fire spread uncontrollably, affecting 34 other shacks. 
The successive fire outbreaks have hardly received a lot of support out of NGO which was limited following available resources. As such, the recent fire above has not yet receive government assistance which was expected on shelter early recovery or long-term solutions. There has been reported claims and violent incidents from the previous fire affected communities that needs to be consider. The population is calling for an assistance in chronological order and has shown and expressed the sensitivity related to the planned distribution of authorities in the recent fires while previous still need to be assisted in one way or another. 

As of the latest update, relief efforts are ongoing by SARCS on the first fire incident and team is also deployed in Johannesburg to provide aid, hot meal and support to those impacted by the disaster. 
In Johannesburg as done during the KwaZulu Natal fire, SARCS deployed a team that continues to collaborate with government disaster management teams to conduct assessments. SARCS will be providing Psychosocial Support (PSS), Restoring of Family Links RFL (services which include (Free phone call services, Tracing and case management. More services which include food, clothing, blankets, mattresses will be provided to affected people.

response_strategy:
The operational strategy rationale seek to address the needs that have been identified during the Rapid Needs assessment in Kwa zULU and Johannesburg following the fire incidents. To address the needs of the affected people this DREF was launched to rolling out immediate response interventions to address shelter, health, WASH, livelihoods and basic needs of the affected people. The Following intervention pillars were set and will be maintain and extended to Johannesburg response following the second fire outbreak on 30.08.2023:
• Detailed assessments in the affected area already conducted and recover through this allocation.
• Immediate relief which includes blankets, mattresses and hot meals.
• Provision of Smoke detectors/alarms.
• Provision of kitchen kits.
• Support access to food in the sites for at least 5 weeks.
• Facilitate PSS. 
• Capacity building and sensitization to 20 volunteers on CVA, fire awareness, PGI and CEA.
• Visibility materials and protective clothing for operation response team.
• Strengthen and continue the advocacy among relevant stakeholders on the fire prevention, sustainable solutions and reliable mechanism to reduce these outbreaks.
• Scale-up awareness campaigns on fire incidents and health risk in the evacuation centers and host communities with benefit of trained team and appropriate printing of IEC material to reduce the impact of future fires and mitigate the risk of water related and others diseases.
• Ensure Multi-purpose cash to the people affected in the Johannesburg fire and support with awareness on the use of cash for priority immediate needs. The Cash process will be inclusive of communities and process through a cash-card modality. Secured card will be issued and convert into either cash or items in identified shops. Families that will receive the card will have the flexibility to: 
- Withdrawal of cash and then buy any specific items in any of their preferred markets/shops or process with rental or others priority needs.
- Exchange the Card into food items, shelter or other items in some identified shops of the NS.
Shops identified will be part of a chain store across Johannesburg and they are already working with the NS. This process has already been successfully used by the NS for others assistance. It is also more sensitive on the ongoing complaints and help mitigate the security/protection issues that are usually faced through mobile money. 
SARCS has ensure coordination with local authorities to address the existing complaints. A Workshop on advocacy with partners on shelter and urban fire management and shelter solutions will be organize to have clear actions forward. Dynamic being different and administrations being different, two discussions need to take place with relevant parties to enable right decision making.
Aside from that, SARCS will continue strengthen the community engagement through community discussion, promotion of acceptance and understanding of neutrality of the planned intervention. 

• Monitor and advocate on the shelter assistance scale-up in Kennedy.

These being more or less a repetitive incident, the country team will explore how to engage with partners involve in fire incident management in the country, especially in the affected areas to see how to set up mechanism for preventing and early actions/response to fire that will avoid such impact in the communities. NS is engaged on advocacy with stakeholders and local authorities that aim at scaling-up :
(i)	Engagement with National disaster management agency and civil protection to potentially envisage the creation & training of fire management committee teams that can rapidly prevent & respond to fire outbreak. 
(ii)	Advocacy and collaboration on possible innovative ways to prevent fire outbreak (Fire sensors, planning evacuation routes, participatory sessions with the community) to significantly reduce fire incidents. IFRC to contribute through the presence of a surge to bring technical guidance and actions plans - immediate and long term.
(iii)   Engagement with Government and IFRC for respective administrative and technical support to identified and set up under an urban risk reduction program actions to address this risk.
(iv) The educative sessions are also planned to be conducted in the communities in coordination with Department of social development and fire services for fire risk sensitizations, consequences, prevention, community system and early actions.

The shelter and livelihood assistance are limited for now to the immediate life saving measures with consideration of possible support from Government and others partners for a more sustainable solution. Department of Human settlement following the response process with displaced population, will specify relocation sites before any further assistance planned.  NS include under this intervention to continue the coordination and advocacy with regular meetings with Government and DHS for a coordinated long term and safety solution. 

It is important to note that this incident is in urban areas in Kwazulu, not far from a main road and lacking for now clear position of local authorities on long term shelter assistance. Hence, the NS will provide the immediate households items to mitigate the risk of diseases and support to enhance the hygiene conditions. However, when the Government will advise on the safe relocation site/place, the NS could revise and include a more complete assistance. 

However, in the meantime, SARCS will increase the livability, privacy & protection of the collective halls which are hosting displaced families with improvement of WASH assistance that address also the protection concern. Based on the rapid assessment done on 25th July 2023, NS included some gender segregated and accessible mobile toilets/WASH facilities.
people_assisted:
Under DREF SARCS is targeting to reach 2,790 people, 1,388 affected households of which 1,213 are the one affected in Kennedy Road and 175 affected in Johannesburg.

With all the people affected being in the sites, it is crucial to avoid creating conflict as all the affected families are homeless and also with consideration of sensitivity and claims from host communities on the plan of assistance to the migrants affected in Johannesburg. Align with the RCRC humanitarian principle and the scope of the DREF tool, SARCS will then provide equitable assistance to the Johannesburg families through MPC and keep the initial relief assistance planned in Kennedy that is agreed with communities. 

People that are staying in shelters are the ones who will receive more support because they are the one identified and registered in the shelters and can be verified. Although the government has profiled citizens for potential relief the situation on the ground is sensitive if specific interventions from non-governmental organizations might segregate between citizens and non-citizens. There is a threat for social unrest and there is need for response interventions to target all affected people.
operation_objective: This DREF allocation aims to support 2,779 people that lost their homes on the fire incident happen in Kennedy Road informal settlement in KwaZulu Natal and Johannesburg building fire with urgent assistance in livelihoods and basic needs (food, blankets, mattresses, clothes etc.), WASH (hygiene packs and sanitary towels) and shelter support (smoke alarms, kitchen kits etc) as well as fire prevention and advocacy for relevant solution beyond the 6 months of this DREF.

event_description:
In South Africa, unstructured fires are on the rise in the informal settlements especially in this winter season. 
The fire that blazed one of the five-Storey dilapidated buildings in Johannesburg CBD earliest hours on the 31st of August 2023 left about 175 households which were hosting about 422 people immense plight to meet their basic needs. From BBC information, at least 76 fatalities have been recorded, search and rescue services still continue as some bodies are believed to be still trapped inside the building. The Johannesburg Metro indicated that the building was invaded as it was disregarded of not meeting the standards of safe shelter due to its dilapidated state. 

This fire outbreak come after reported fires incidents also in Durben. Indeed, on 16th of July 2023, a fire incident was already reported in the KwaZulu Natal province, specifically on Kennedy Road informal settlement. This caused adverse impact leaving 2,357 people (647 children and 1710 adults) displaced with almost all their belongings swept away by the strong fire. https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-66215286. 
Following the report from Disaster Management Centre confirming the incident and rapid assessment conducted by the NS, SARCS has activated response team to assist with KwaZulu Natal province fire response. IFRC supported the scale-up of the SARCS initiated assistance through an allocation of CHF 214,419 allowing to extend their response capacity to the expressed needs in the different evacuation centers. The recent outbreak in Johannesburg require now to deploy same humanitarian services to the affected communities that are also leave without any substantial assistance week after the fire outbreak.

needs_identified.description:
At community level, this situation created mosquito niches and factors conducive to diarrheic diseases and other diseases related to dirty water. The risk of disease/epidemic to occur was  prevented. The sensitization of communities was an immediate priority.
The destruction of infrastructure and the management of debris exposed communities to the risk of injury.

needs_identified.title: water_sanitation_and_hygiene
needs_identified.description:
The rains were violent and rapid, washing away roads, garbage and community structures. According to information received from the provincial Red Cross committee, several drainage channels were destroyed, creating a high-risk environment for households, especially children and vulnerable groups. In addition, the reservoirs of rainwater naturally created by the absence of run-offs due to the transported debris limited environmental hygiene conditions and fostered vector niches.

A number of households that had found refuge with host families were also in need of ongoing household hygiene support, helping to prevent water-borne diseases and poor hygiene.

Immediate access to drinking water is also necessary for these households, for whom some of the water supply routes normally used have been cut off or damaged by the winds, or whose wells and boreholes have simply become cloudy during the rainy season or have received significant debris, and require measures to clean up and stabilize the quality of the water.

As the government was committed in restoring the infrastructure, the GRC first ensured immediate access to drinking water by supplying water treatment equipment.

needs_identified.title: shelter_housing_and_settlements
needs_identified.description: According to data collected by the NS branches up to the 18th May, 200 houses were damaged by the winds in Franceville and its vicinity. These homes were either inhabitable or too risky for families to move into. The debris also damaged household equipment. With no other options, many households keep living in their homes or in neighboring host households.

planned_interventions.progress_towards_outcome:
The procedures for deploying the Surge took almost 2 weeks from the date of the DREF's approval.  
The Surge arrived in Libreville on 23 June 2023 and began supporting the NS with training, preparation of the multi-sector evaluation mission (development of ToRs, questionnaires and coordination with the Provincial Committee).
The Cluster's CVA Officer arrived in Libreville on 23 June 2023. In the meantime, the Cluster's CVA Officer provided remote support for the development of the ToRs for the multi-sectoral evaluation, the cash feasibility study (including the agreement with the financial service provider who had signed a contract with the SN) and the ToRs and questions for the market study. The Cluster's CVA Officer also provided technical support for capacity building for NS staff and volunteers on cash.
- The finance manager in charge of this operation went on a support mission to the Gabonese RC at the start of this operation and provided the NS programme and finance team with support through a finance briefing on the GRC procedures manual and an explanation of the checklist. The checklist is a file containing all the documents needed to justify the various expenses incurred in implementing GRC projects. This checklist helped the NS to collect the necessary documents for expenditure or disbursement of funds.
Before the effective start of the DREF violent winds operations, the cluster logistician, during his visit to Gabon as part of the DREF Marburg, provided technical support to the NS in Gabon for logistical procedures. PMER also provided support for the development of a DREF monitoring plan in July 2023. As part of the support provided to the DREF team, the cluster program manager carried out a mission to support the NS's activities, in particular a meeting with the PSF to refine the strategy for distributing cash to beneficiaries and transporting NFIs to Franceville.
In addition, the IFRC continued to provide remote support and local follow-up to the CRG as part of this operation. Monitoring meetings were initiated and held every day until the electoral period, when they had to be stopped due to the interruption of the internet connection in Gabon. Nevertheless, monitoring continued via telephone calls.

summary_of_change:
This DREF's activities were implemented in accordance with the chronogram shared. Operations had to be carried out before the start of the electoral campaign on 11 August 2023. The following activities were achieved by that date:
- Training of volunteers.
- Needs assessment> 
- Awareness-raising activities (PGI, CEA, WASH).
- Distribution of NFIs to approximately 70% of target. 
However, the following events delayed the implementation: 
- Delay in the transfer of funds from the IFRC to the financial service providers due to malfunctions of the banking services, causing a significant delay in the distribution of cash.
- Elections: in view of the campaign and the approach of the elections date, the National Society suspended all activities, not only to avoid any confusion between the activities of the RC and political activities, but also to avoid any possible risk of staff and volunteers being exposed to violence.
- Coup d'état: Given the current socio-political context in the country following the coup d'état on 30 August, it was necessary to anticipate by requesting an extension of the implementation timeframe for this operation given the different scenarios developed.

Due to these delays, the NS is requesting a 2-month extension and an addition of CHF 24,168 to:
- Carry out the remaining distributions: distribution of blankets and other HHI.
- Distribution of cash transfers.
- Sensitizations on health etc.
- Carry out PDM and lessons learned workshop.
The additional funds we are requesting will permit the NS to:
- Extend the costs of field monitoring missions (NS and cluster office) given that the previous missions lasted longer than expected for circumstances beyond control on the field.
- Insert cost for the cash PDM which had not been taken into account in the initial budget.
- Increase communication costs (IFRC and NS) for the duration of the extension and in view of the almost daily follow-up with the NS.
- Readjust the costs of the lessons learned workshop due to fluctuating cost of air tickets between Franceville and Libreville, given that air travel is the only option presently available.
- Extend the Surge's mission for one more month to finalize the remaining activities.
identified_gaps:
The areas affected are urban and peri-urban localities in which most households would already like to start rebuilding but are financially blocked. 
Considering the challenges faced due to accessibility, the type of population affected (mostly urban) and the plurality of needs, a cash approach was the most effective way of addressing the needs already expressed and those anticipated. Unfortunately, although GRC has a contract with a mobile company, this contract does not extend to cash but could be considered. 
To guarantee assistance that remains relevant to communities, the cash or in-kind support approach considered the rapidity of implementation.
icrc: There is no ICRC action that has been received so far.
selection_criteria: The local administrative authorities supported by the NS local disaster response team visited the affected areas and pre-estimated the number of people in need at 1,818 disaster victims.
ifrc:
The IFRC Cluster Office based in Yaoundé held a meeting with the NS to get more information on the situation in the aﬀected region. Support was given to post an alert on the GO Platform and a Cluster team was activated to assist the NS in developing a response plan.
The IFRC Cluster had also carried out several support missions for the Gabonese RC including:
- Deployment of surge.
- The mission of the finance manager and cash manager.
- The Program missions.
These various missions provided support for volunteer training, multi-sector needs assessments, market analysis and technical support for finance and the program.
In addition to these missions, weekly online monitoring meetings are held with the cluster and NS team, followed by daily meetings for closer monitoring.
risk_security_concern:
All staff were equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE). Teams made sure they didn't go beyond the security perimeter. A rescue team was deployed and daily brieﬁngs and debrieﬁngs were conducted. Given that Franceville is 700 km from Libreville, the main accessible means was by railroad. However, this route was closed for passenger transportation for over a month following a landslide on one section. As the road network is not developed, the only means accessible to Franceville was by air, which was very expensive.

To reduce the risk of RCRC personnel falling victim to crime, violence or road hazards active risk mitigation measures were adopted. Security orientation and briefing for all teams prior to deployment was also undertaken to help ensure the safety and security of response teams. Standard security protocols about general norms, cultural sensitivity and an overall code of conduct was put in place. Minimum-security requirements was strictly maintained. All National Society and IFRC personnel actively involved in the operations successfully completed prior to deployment the respective IFRC security e-learning courses (i.e., Level 1 Fundamentals, Level 2 Personal and Volunteer Security and Level 3 Security for Managers). IFRC security plans applied to all IFRC staff throughout the operation. Area specific Security Risk Assessment was conducted for any operational area should any IFRC personnel be deployed there; risk mitigation measures were identified and implemented.
national_authorities: Officials from the Haut Ogooué Governor's office visited the area to assess the situation. According to a press release signed by the Prime Minister on 15th May 2023, the President of the Republic had instructed the Government to visit Franceville from 17th to 18th May 2023 to provide aid and assistance to the victims, as well as assess the extent of the damage and explore ways and means to remedy them. No detail information has been given on the nature of the assistance to be provided and the number of people who will be assisted by the authorities.
communication: To foster the visibility of GRC actions, the NS made the most use of its media pages, mainly on social media. Strategic meetings with local leaders and authorities also helped to promote NS actions, volunteers in their mission and the visibility of Red Cross actions in the field.
surge_personnel_deployed: A disaster management resource person/surge with expertise in program evaluation and management was deployed to support the National Society in the assessment and implementation. This deployment lasted for 3 months. At the Yaoundé cluster level, technical support for the development of assessment tools and the analysis of the information collected was provided by all sectors.
